clue.text: Ask me inside to supervise kids

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for me sits within the word for ask

parts.note: to ask someone along is to invite them
the setter of this puzzle is Gila, so me stands for that name

explanation.surface: Someone is being asked to come in and keep an eye on the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the setter speaking: setters often use me or I for their own pseudonym, here Gila.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigilate is to oversee students sitting an exam, a supervisory job over young people.

clue.text: Networking site where popular snappers primarily tag stuff

parts.note: something popular is in, fashionable

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word snappers

parts.note: to stuff is to cram or ram in

explanation.surface: A description of a photo-sharing app where keen photographers label their pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Instagram is a well-known social media platform for sharing photographs.

clue.text: Girl is upset when stationed in horrible little place

indicators.note: stationed in says one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: horrible means vile

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is unhappy about being posted to an awful small town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like emotional distress, but in a down clue it turns the word over.
explanation.definitionFit: A village is a small settlement, a modest community smaller than a town.

clue.text: Old courtyard protected by King Arthur

indicators.note: protected by says the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A historic yard was once guarded by the legendary King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: A garth is an archaic term for an enclosed yard or cloister garden.

clue.text: It takes a time to follow most of recent court summons

indicators.note: to follow means the other pieces come after the shortened word
most of means drop the final letter of the word for recent

parts.note: recent means late, as in the late news
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone receives a legal writ that arrives a little time after recent events.
explanation.definitionFit: A latitat was an old writ summoning a defendant to the King's Bench court.

clue.text: Joyrider wrote the fronts of classic cars off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are muddled
the fronts of asks for the first letters of classic and cars

explanation.surface: A joyrider wrote off a string of classic cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' mixes WROTE with CC from the fronts of 'classic cars'.
explanation.definitionFit: A twoccer is British slang for someone who Takes Without Owner's Consent, i.e. a car thief.

clue.text: A few reflective, brooding music fans

indicators.note: reflective suggests a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a few means some

explanation.surface: Some fans of moody music are in a thoughtful frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Emo followers like intense, emotional rock and a gloomy look, hence brooding.

clue.text: Drink obtained from a market in Italy

parts.note: a mart is a market
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A drink bought at an Italian market.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: British band rocked on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard spoken rather than seen

parts.note: rocked means swayed back and forth

explanation.surface: A British group played rock music in a radio session.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede are an English rock band from the Britpop era led by Brett Anderson.

clue.text: Cardinal has rather restricted vision

indicators.note: restricted means held in by the number word

parts.note: a cardinal number such as eight
rather! is an old-fashioned way of saying yes emphatically

explanation.surface: A senior churchman's sight is somewhat limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman but is a cardinal number, EIGHT, holding YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, synonymous with vision.

clue.text: Lead characters in sitcoms often laugh at readers of The Sun

indicators.note: lead characters means the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Tabloid readers of The Sun newspaper are said to laugh at sitcoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun' looks like the British tabloid, but the definition is about our star.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to the sun in the sky.

clue.text: Rock band's front man took rhyme for re-composition

indicators.note: re-composition means writing the letters out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer took a rhyme in order to rewrite a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Thom Yorke is the lead singer of the English rock band Radiohead.

clue.text: A way to refer to being upset without showing emotion

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: upset means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to refer to a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: Someone describes a way to talk about distress without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the emotion but turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic describes someone indifferent and showing no feeling or interest.

clue.text: Lead singer of band missing last part of tour

indicators.note: missing means one letter is taken away

parts.note: a stripe is a band of colour

indicators.note: last part of means the final letter of the word tour

explanation.surface: A band's lead singer skips the end of a concert tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a music group but is a stripe of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Stipe was the lead vocalist of the American rock group R.E.M.

clue.text: Choose another time to take part in degree lectures

indicators.note: take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A student decides once more to attend lectures for a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect is to vote someone into office again, choosing them a second time.

clue.text: Demanding old partner putting on a performance

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
acting is putting on a performance

explanation.surface: A former partner is being difficult while playing a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means making strict demands, requiring great effort or care.

clue.text: Music newspaper and a news magazine

parts.note: rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
Time is a weekly American news magazine

explanation.surface: A newspaper and a magazine about music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano style popular around 1900, played by Scott Joplin.

clue.text: Eastern Portugal had epic bursts of weather

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

indicators.note: bursts means the words break apart and recombine

explanation.surface: Eastern Portugal experienced dramatic downpours.
explanation.definitionFit: Epedaphic is a rare term for conditions depending on climate, relating to atmospheric conditions.

clue.text: Gas meter almost broken by workman…almost

indicators.note: broken by means a second piece is inserted into the first
almost means the final letter of meter is dropped
the second almost cuts the last letter from the word for workman

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A gas meter has nearly been broken by a workman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' twice: METE (meter shortened) is broken by HAN (hand shortened).
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a flammable hydrocarbon, the main component of natural fuel gas.

clue.text: Place from which to get good speed and better drugs

definitions.text: Place from which to get good speed

parts.note: to better is to top or surpass
gear is slang for illegal drugs

explanation.surface: A dealer's pitch: where to find good speed and superior narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like the drug but is velocity, reached in a car's highest gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Top gear is the highest ratio in a vehicle, giving maximum speed.

clue.text: Rubbish mince pie was hard

parts.note: mince pie is Cockney rhyming slang for eye
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a mince pie was tough and inedible.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'mince pies' are eyes, so a mince pie is an EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash means nonsense or claptrap, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Entertainer performing satire about Tory leader

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece
performing suggests the letters are made to act differently, rearranged
leader means the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: A comic performs a satirical sketch about the head of the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' turns SATIRE into ARTISE, put about T.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Last piece of pineapple in crushed tin can is well out-of-date

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece
crushed means the letters are squashed into a new order
last piece of means the final letter of pineapple

explanation.surface: A tin of pineapple with its last chunk left in is long past its use-by date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' makes ANCINT from TIN CAN, with E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, long past being current.

clue.text: Stop bringing up endless row about things that are of little value

indicators.note: about means wrapped round another piece
bringing up in a down clue reverses the word
endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a row is a loud noise

parts.words: things that are of little value
parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless stuff

explanation.surface: Someone stops raising a pointless argument about trivial things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter, then 'bringing up' reverses what is left (SION) before it goes round the cheap stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is a stopping place for trains or buses.

clue.text: Former postman living abroad

parts.note: ex means former
Postman Pat is a British children's TV character

explanation.surface: A retired postman now resides overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a well-known British children's TV series about a village postman.
explanation.definitionFit: Expat, short for expatriate, describes someone residing outside their native country.

clue.text: The limits of a rock guitarist?

definitions.meaning: belonging to The Edge, the guitarist of the band U2, written possessively

explanation.surface: A question about the boundaries of a rock musician's talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges are limits or borders; read as a possessive it is U2's guitarist The Edge.

clue.text: Spicy food — a nice dhal, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An example of spicy cooking: a pleasant lentil curry.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling and covered in chilli sauce.

clue.text: Cake decoration made from infused cream is no good at first

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A cake topping made with flavoured cream turns out badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on top of cakes.

clue.text: Fruit is good to hold once more

parts.note: to re-engage is to take up or hold again

explanation.surface: A fruit is said to be good for keeping again.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a sweet green variety of plum.

clue.text: Personal assistant returns with husband from Dublin perhaps

indicators.note: returns means the name is read back to front

parts.note: Siri is Apple's virtual personal assistant

explanation.surface: A PA comes back with her husband, perhaps from Ireland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal assistant' is not a secretary but Apple's voice assistant Siri.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Dublin is Irish, Dublin being Ireland's capital.

clue.text: Kind person

definitions.meaning: an individual, as in a good type of fellow

explanation.surface: A short phrase describing a generous individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Sort means a type or variety, and also a person of a given character, as in a good egg.

clue.text: Attractive doctor got nice Vietnamese dish as a starter

indicators.note: as a starter means the dish comes first, before the rest

parts.note: pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor ordered a nice Vietnamese soup to begin the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb, rearranging GOT NICE into TOGENIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Photogenic means looking good in photographs, hence attractive.
